findings.detail: PromptPieceTokenStore keeps scoped piece token IDs in RAM with no TTL, only a byte-bounded two-generation eviction. A cached prefix saves roughly 0.1-0.35 s of tokenization for 27-46K-token prompts, a much larger signal than a KV hit. Within one cache scope a caller can probe whether a known prefix was recently submitted. The signal can outlive the 30-minute sliding TTL that T-041 and SEC-035 assume for prefix reuse. It lasts until eviction or tokenizer unload, and it applies even when the KV prefix cache declines a donation (adoption, benefit, endurance or disk guards). Cross-account leakage is prevented by the scope-keyed SHA-256, assuming the coordinator authors the scope. The T-041 and SEC-035 acceptance does not cover this second oracle. Fix: add a TTL to the piece store matching the prefix-cache TTL, or record this oracle explicitly in T-041 and SEC-035. The scope must stay coordinator-derived, and nil or empty scopes must take the unchanged path.
findings.title: Prompt-token cache adds a same-scope tokenization timing oracle outside T-041's 30-minute TTL bound
